prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1181; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a side impact at a signalized intersection and provided a consistent account of how the other vehicle entered the junction. Police and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both match the described impact, and the damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with a side strike. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Claimant has reported a wrist fracture, but it is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash. Medical records are requested to confirm the diagnosis and the mechanism of injury.

Entry 4: Treatment so far has followed a usual course, with the claimant attending follow-up visits that became less frequent as the wrist improved. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the information gathered to date.

Entry 5: Each time the claimant has been contacted, the account of the collision has stayed the same in its key details. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been answering questions directly.

Entry 6: Current status: liability and vehicle damage appear established, while the causation question for the wrist injury remains open pending the medical records. Next step is to review the records and schedule a follow-up with the claimant.
